ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

rockwood — pattern 4

Following a direct shoulder injury, an axillary view shows the distal clavicle displaced posteriorly into the trapezius. The deformity is not primarily inferior displacement or merely an increase in vertical coracoclavicular distance. The AC stabilizing ligaments are disrupted. Which Rockwood acromioclavicular injury type best fits this pattern?

  1. Type IV
  2. Type V
  3. Type VI
  4. Type I
  5. Type II
Answer and explanation

Type IV

Type IV: Posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius.

Option explanations

Type IV: Type IV: Posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius.

Type V: Type V describes marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%. The case instead matches Type IV.

Type VI: Type VI describes inferior displacement of the distal clavicle, beneath the acromion or coracoid. The case instead matches Type IV.

Type I: Type I describes an AC ligament sprain with intact coracoclavicular ligaments and no radiographic displacement. The case instead matches Type IV.

Type II: Type II describes aC ligament disruption with coracoclavicular ligament sprain and mild displacement. The case instead matches Type IV.
